Sandbox_Storm_ServerFps: Server FPS (tick rate + lockFps + physics FPS)
Sandbox_Storm_ServerFps_tooltip: Unified server FPS. Drives the main-loop tick gate (1000/fps ms), PerformanceSettings.getLockFPS() on the server, and the IsoPhysicsObject.update() FPS scalar — all three together. 10 = vanilla 10 TPS. Higher = faster simulation but more CPU.
Sandbox_Storm_AnimalLOSTickInterval_tool: Per-animal stride for IsoAnimal.updateLOS(). 1 = vanilla every-tick. Larger = each animal scans LOS every Nth tick (cheaper). 0 disables LOS entirely. Animal-sourced Tracking/Sneak/Nimble/Lightfoot XP only awards from this scan, so stride N also divides that XP by N (0 = none).
Sandbox_Storm_VirtualAnimalTickInterval_: Stride for the whole AnimalZones.updateVirtualAnimals() pass (off-screen animal movement, eat/sleep, track expiry). 1 = vanilla every-tick. Larger = the pass runs every Nth tick and compensates by advancing simulated time N ticks at once, so animals cover the same ground but in coarser steps (map track overlay looks jumpier at high values). 0 freezes virtual-animal simulation and track expiry entirely — debug/emergency use only.
Sandbox_Storm_ZombieAuthTickInterval_too: Per-zombie stride for the ownership rescan of UNOWNED zombies in NetworkZombieManager.updateAuth(). Vanilla rescans every unowned zombie against every connection's players every single tick; with N > 1 each unowned zombie rescans every Nth tick instead. Owned zombies keep vanilla's 2-second gate, so handoff between nearby players is unaffected. Worst case a newly relevant zombie waits N-1 extra ticks for an owner (1.5 s at the ceiling of 16 on a 10 TPS server). 1 = vanilla.
Sandbox_Storm_InventoryItemSweepTickInte: Stride for the orphaned-item entity sweep in InventoryItemSystem.update(). The sweep is pure garbage collection (unregisters items whose equip parent is gone or dead) and idempotent, so striding it only delays cleanup by up to N-1 ticks. 1 = vanilla every-tick; ceiling 64 (6.4 s between sweeps at 10 TPS).
Sandbox_Storm_MaxTotalZombies_tooltip: Hard ceiling on the number of real zombies loaded across the WHOLE map at once. Vanilla has no such cap: ZombieConfig.ZombiesCountBeforeDelete only limits how many zombies are streamed to one connection, MaxZombiesPerChunk only bounds a single chunk, so the world total grows without limit as more players spread out — and the per-tick zombie ownership scan costs scale with that total. When the world exceeds this number, Storm deletes the surplus at up to 200 zombies per second, choosing only zombies nobody can see (outside, no target, not a reanimated player, and beyond every connection's relevance radius) — the same safety conditions vanilla's own per-connection cull uses. If not enough zombies qualify, the world stays over the cap rather than deleting one a player could notice. Deleted zombies re-enter the normal respawn schedule, so a cap set below what your population settings want produces constant churn: watch storm_zombies_total_cap_culled_total, and if it never settles, lower ZombieConfig.PopulationMultiplier instead of raising this. 0 = disabled (vanilla behaviour, no global cap).
Sandbox_Storm_ServerLosThreads_tooltip: Number of concurrent player LOS scans per tick. 1 = vanilla single-threaded baseline. Up to 16. The helper pool always pre-allocates 15 threads regardless; this knob only controls how many receive work each tick.
Sandbox_Storm_NetDataCapMs_tooltip: Per-outer-loop-spin wall-clock cap on time spent inside GameServer.mainLoopDealWithNetData (HIGH-priority + player-update + vehicle inbound drain combined). Default 90. When a spin exceeds the cap, subsequent packets in that spin are dropped at the application level (already ACKed — RakNet does not retransmit them; the periodic update streams regenerate the state); the next spin starts fresh. Protects world-tick scheduling and the RakNet outbound send buffer during reconnect storms. 0 = disabled (vanilla behaviour, no cap). Counter: pz_netdata_deferred_total.
Sandbox_Storm_PeerSendBufferKickMb: Auto-kick peer when HIGH send buffer exceeds (MB, 0 = disabled)
Sandbox_Storm_PeerSendBufferKickMb_toolt: If a peer's outbound HIGH-priority RakNet send buffer stays above this many megabytes for Storm.PeerSendBufferKickHoldTicks consecutive ticks, Storm force-disconnects the connection with reason storm-send-buffer-overflow. Protects the server from OOM when a peer on a saturated or lossy uplink accumulates the server's broadcast firehose in their per-peer RakNet queue (PZ has no backpressure anywhere in the HIGH-priority send paths, so a stalled peer otherwise grows unbounded until OOM). Default 20 MB. 0 = disabled (no auto-kick). Per-peer gauge: storm_peer_send_buffer_bytes{priority="high"}. Counter: storm_peer_kicked_send_buffer_total.
Sandbox_Storm_PeerSendBufferKickHoldTick: Send-buffer kick hold ticks (consecutive ticks above threshold)

Number of consecutive server ticks a peer's HIGH send buffer must stay above Storm.PeerSendBufferKickMb before Storm force-disconnects them. At the vanilla 10 TPS, 50 ticks = 5 seconds (default). Lower values fire faster but risk false-positiving brief broadcast spikes; higher values give more grace before action. Range 1-6000 (≈10 min at 10 TPS). Has no effect when Storm.PeerSendBufferKickMb = 0 (watchdog disabled).
Sandbox_Storm_ScreenshotPiecesPerPacket_: Number of base64 pieces (24573 raw bytes each) packed into a single sendClientCommand packet when a client uploads a /screenshot back to the server. This is only wire framing (packet size), NOT the upload throttle — disconnect safety is governed by Storm.ScreenshotUploadKbPerSec. Fewer, larger packets mean fewer sendClientCommand calls. Default 4 (~131 KB/packet). Hard ceiling 28 (~918 KB/packet, vanilla UdpConnection's 1 MB outbound buffer cap with ~82 KB headroom); above that the ByteBufferWriter throws BufferOverflowException mid-send.
Sandbox_Storm_ScreenshotUploadKbPerSec_t: Wall-clock throughput cap on how fast a client streams a captured /screenshot back to the server, in KiB/s of base64 wire bytes. This is the disconnect fix: the upload must stay well under the player's uplink so RakNet's ACK/keepalive traffic keeps flowing. If the upload outruns the uplink, the reliable send backlog grows past RakNet's ~10 s connection timeout and the player is dropped with Connection Lost — and that backlog scales with screenshot resolution, which is why players on large monitors were disconnected. Default 128 KiB/s (~1 Mbit), safe on virtually any home uplink; raise it on low-latency wired networks for faster uploads. A full-resolution 4K screenshot may take a minute or more to upload at the default — this is invisible to the player and runs in the background.
Sandbox_Storm_ScreenshotEncodeKbPerTick_: Maximum source KiB base64-encoded per client tick while uploading a /screenshot. This is the client-lag fix: base64 runs on the single Lua main thread, so encoding a whole piece per frame stalled rendering for the entire upload. Encoding is also demand-driven (it pauses once enough packets are buffered ahead of the throttled sender), so with a small budget most ticks do little or no work. Default 4 KiB/tick. Lower = smoother frames but slower to fill each packet; higher = faster encode but larger per-frame hitches.
Sandbox_Storm_ReapStalledConnectionSecon: Wall-clock budget a connection gets to finish logging in AND spawn a character before Storm drops it and frees its RakNet slot (half of the "Getting Server Info..." fix). Fully-connected players are never touched, and time spent in the login queue, awaiting co-op approval, pending Google auth, or actively downloading chunks re-stamps the clock and does not count — so a slow link cannot get a client kicked mid-load. Default 600 (10 minutes), range 60-7200. Ignored when -Dstorm.reapStalledConnectionMs is set on the server JVM: the launch flag always wins over this option. Gauge: storm_connection_reap_timeout_seconds.
Sandbox_Storm_ZombieSightVehicleFastPath: Fast vehicle check for zombie sight

Speeds up the test for whether a vehicle blocks a zombie's line of sight. Vehicles block sight either way and no zombie is ever removed — this only changes how the check is computed. Vanilla checks every vehicle in the loaded world (two matrix inversions each) for every zombie sight roll, even when the result cannot matter; with this enabled Storm only tests vehicles near the zombie-to-target line and skips the test entirely when the spot chance is already zero. ~14%% of main-thread CPU on vehicle-heavy servers. Disable to restore the vanilla scan when diagnosing zombie-spotting oddities. Gauge: storm_zombie_sight_vehicle_fast_path.
Sandbox_Storm_PlayerLosFastPath_tooltip: Speeds up each player's per-tick line-of-sight scan over the loaded world's moving objects. Zombies spot players, panic/boredom build-up, and everything else the server acts on are computed exactly as vanilla — this only skips objects too far away to possibly be visible (outside the 96x96-square visibility window) and client-only bookkeeping (fade-in alpha, music-intensity counters, jump-scare state) that a dedicated server never reads. ~18%% of main-thread CPU on a full server. Disable to restore the vanilla scan when diagnosing spotting or panic oddities. Gauge: storm_player_los_fast_path.
Sandbox_Storm_UsingPlayerSweepFastPath_t: Speeds up the per-tick check that releases a crafting station / butcher hook / build window when the player using it walks away, changes floor, or dies. Vanilla scans every world-object entity (100k+ on a busy server) each tick to find the handful actually in use; with this enabled Storm keeps a small registry of in-use objects and checks only those, releasing them under exactly the vanilla rules (player outside a 10-tile box, different floor, or dead). ~6%% of main-thread CPU on a full server. Safe to toggle live in either direction — the registry is maintained even while disabled. Disable to restore the vanilla scan when diagnosing stuck 'in use by another player' objects. Gauge: storm_using_player_sweep_fast_path.
Sandbox_Storm_FluidContainerUpdateFastPa: Speeds up the 100ms simulation pass over every fluid container (rain collectors, petrol containers). Rain collection, snow, petrol evaporation, and network sync happen exactly as vanilla — this only reads the weather and day-length settings once per pass instead of once per container, checks the cheap conditions first so containers that cannot collect rain or evaporate petrol are skipped without scanning their fluid list, and compares the petrol fluid by identity instead of by string. ~6%% of main-thread CPU on a full server. Disable to restore the vanilla pass when diagnosing fluid oddities. Gauge: storm_fluid_container_update_fast_path.
Sandbox_Storm_EcsClassCache_tooltip: Caches the result of the ECS component-class walk that vanilla recomputes on every component lookup (millions of times per second on a busy server — every state-machine and AI access per character per tick). The walk is a pure function of the class, so the cached answer is always identical to vanilla's. ~3%% of main-thread CPU on a full server. Always safe to toggle live. Disable to restore the vanilla walk. Gauge: storm_ecs_class_cache.
Sandbox_Storm_CellUnloadBudgetPerTick: Max map-cell unloads per tick (0 = vanilla, unlimited)
Sandbox_Storm_CellUnloadBudgetPerTick_to: Caps how many stale map cells (64x64-square server cells nobody is near anymore) the server destructively unloads in a single tick. Vanilla unloads every stale cell at once, so several players logging off or driving away together turns into one multi-hundred-ms tick spike — each cell unload walks 64 chunks and unregisters every entity in them. With a budget, cells beyond the cap simply stay loaded and are re-checked next tick (a cell that becomes relevant again is kept; a stale one is unloaded a few ticks later), spreading the burst over multiple ticks. Everything about each unload — saving, pathfind pause, zombie/animal virtualization — is exactly vanilla; only the number per tick changes. Default 2; ceiling 32. Set 0 to restore vanilla unload-everything-now behaviour. Counter: pz_server_cell_unloads_total. Gauge: storm_cell_unload_budget_per_tick.
Sandbox_Storm_EntityRemoveFastPath_toolt: Speeds up unregistering entities from the engine's global entity list. Vanilla scans the whole list (123k+ entities on a busy server) to find each entity being removed — the dominant per-entity cost when chunks unload. Storm keeps an identity index of every entity's position and removes in O(1), verifying the indexed slot actually holds that entity before touching it; on any inconsistency it falls back to the vanilla scan permanently, so a wrong removal is impossible. Which entities exist, and the resulting list contents, are identical to vanilla either way. Safe to toggle live in either direction (re-enabling rebuilds the index once). Disable to restore the vanilla scan. Counter: pz_entity_array_removes_total. Gauges: storm_entity_remove_fast_path, storm_entity_index_size.
